title: Transient headroom collapse after autoscaler rollout — containment playbook, RCA and remediation epics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
On 2026-03-10 02:13 UTC a gradual but sustained drop in dedicated-pool headroom was observed for multiple enterprise customers: headroom dropped from ~20% to ~2% across three critical pools over ~7 minutes, resulting in elevated tail latency and queued requests. The incident correlated with a staged autoscaler rollout (config change to the scale_down hysteresis and utilization smoothing algorithm) deployed at 01:58 UTC.

Immediate impact:
- Reduced capacity headroom causing queuing and 95th/99th pct latency spikes for model outputs.
- Affected customers experienced degraded throughput and transient 429s for non-fallback routes.
- Observable metrics: headroom % per-pool, pending-requests, provisioned-gpus, autoscaler-eval-latency; key signal: scale_down window shortened from 5m->45s.

Containment taken (what we did):
1) Rollback: reverted autoscaler config to previous commit (git:github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler@rev-3f9a2d) at 02:07 UTC — immediate reduction in scale_down events.
2) Emergency reserve: triggered emergency-reserve job to provision warm nodes from coldpool (job id: emergency-reserve-20260310-02) which restored ~8–12% headroom within 6 minutes.
3) Traffic policy: enabled cross-pool fallback routing for high-priority customer routes (policy: fallback-weight=0.25) and temporarily disabled non-critical background batch jobs to free capacity.
4) Throttle & circuit: applied temporary global per-customer qps cap (50% of normal) for affected tiers and activated long-tail-latency circuit breaker in the routing layer.
5) Observability: increased sample rate for RPC traces and KV-cache hit telemetry; opened live dashboard (dashboards/redwood/dedicated/incident-512345) and incident channel (#incident-dedicated-autoscale).

What we verified:
- Headroom returned to nominal within 12 minutes of rollback + reserve.
- No data loss or persistent config drift detected.
- Autoscaler telemetry indicated increased scale_down churn during the rollout window; hypothesis confirmed by correlation of evaluator runtimes and policy throttle.

Initial root cause hypothesis (working):
- The rollout introduced a shorter scale_down hysteresis + a smoothing parameter that aggressively decayed target capacity when utilization transiently spiked (synthetic background batch runs amplified signal).
- The shorter window caused oscillatory scale actions (rapid scale-down followed by catch-up) and left pools under-provisioned during bursts.
- Insufficient canary coverage for production-like concurrency distributions and missing guardrail that prevents scale_down below a headroom floor during rollout.

Short-term mitigations (week 0–2):
- Patch autoscaler: revert smoothing parameter change and add a minimum headroom floor (owner: Marcus Chen, estimate: 3).
- Canary enhancement: expand rollout canary to include traffic profiles from three largest enterprise customers and run synthetic spike tests (owner: SRE team, estimate: 5).
- Alerting: add an SLO-backed alert for headroom <5% sustained >2m and autoscaler-churn-rate >3/min (owner: Observability, estimate: 2).
- Runbook: update dedicated-capacity runbook with explicit rollback and emergency-reserve run steps; include checklist for cross-pool fallback routing (owner: Oncall lead, estimate: 2).

Longer-term remediation epics (quarter roadmap):
- Autoscaler hardening epic: improved smoothing algorithm with safety gates, hysteresis tuning per-pool class, and stricter canary gating (owner: Serving Runtime, epic id: ARC-142, estimate: 13).
- Synthetic and chaos testing: integrate periodic stress tests into CI that emulate mixed burst/steady workloads and validate scaling invariants (owner: Reliability Eng, epic id: REL-88, estimate: 8).
- Operator controls: build UI/CLI for manual emergency hedging (pause autoscaler, apply headroom override, force-reserve) and audit logs (owner: Console team, epic id: CON-77, estimate: 8).
- Capacity hedging policy: automatic lightweight headroom reservation for enterprise tiers during rollouts (owner: Product, epic id: PM-213, estimate: 5).

Acceptance criteria for primary fixes:
- No headroom <5% incidents during staged rollout canaries after fixes for 4 consecutive canaries.
- Autoscaler churn metric reduced to <1/min under synthetic spike tests that previously triggered oscillation.
- Runbook steps validated in a runbook rehearsal with SRE and oncall within 2 weeks.

Artifacts & links:
- Git rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/462
- Emergency reserve job logs: https://console.redwood/dedicated/jobs/emergency-reserve-20260310-02/logs
- Incident dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood/in/incident-512345
- Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Runbook+-+Dedicated+Capacity+Incidents
- Postmortem meeting notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1lJ-incident-512345-notes

Open questions / risks:
- Did an unrelated scheduler change increase background batch concurrency and amplify the signal? (investigating by correlating batch job deployments).
- Potential risk: if reserve failover takes >10 minutes for larger pools, customers on the largest models may see SLA-exceeding latency. Need to benchmark reserve speed.

Next steps (owners & ETA):
- Marcus: land minimal autoscaler patch + canary rollback gate by 2026-03-14 (in progress).
- SRE: run targeted synthetic spike tests by 2026-03-16 and report churn metrics.
- Observability: implement headroom alert and dashboard panel by 2026-03-12 (done).
- Console: spec operator hedging controls and mock UI by 2026-03-20.

This ticket will track containment, RCA, and the immediate remediation items. Larger epics will be split into child tickets after the initial RCA is finalized.
